sentences.text:
The instant petition has been filed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 16.01.2020 passed by learned C.J.M.,
Jamshedpur in Complaint Case No.2607 of 2019 whereby and whereunder cognizance of the offence has been taken under Sections 420/ 467/ 468/ 471 & 120B of the Indian Penal Code and accordingly issued summons against the petitioner.
CASE OF COMPLAINANT 2.

The case of the complainant, in brief, is that the complainant is the lawful owner of the land who was in peaceful possession of 4.18 acres of land (Plot no.273 area 1 acre, Plot No.283, area 0.08 acre,
Plot No.297 area 0.68 acre), situated within Mauza- Kashia, Revenue Thana- Ghatsila, Thana No.531, Halka No.09, P.O. & P.S. Chakulia, District- East Singhum fully detailed in complaint petition.
3. The land was originally recorded in the name of Jema Dasi, W/o Siru Nayak in the record of rights which was finally published in the year 1964.
She transferred the land by executing registered sale deed No.8341 dated 28.10.1968 measuring 2.96 acres to one Haradhan Saha.
Further, said Haradhan Saha transferred the land in the year 1976 in favour of complainant and his two elder brothers, namely, Bishambhar Ghatuary and Nishith Ghatuary.
After the said purchase, the land was duly mutated in the name of purchasers vide Mutation Case No.75 of 1979-80 through chain of titles.
4. Further claim of the land, in question is based on a registered sale deed executed by Bhawani Shankar Giri on 19.10.1968 in favour of the complainant.

Complainant claims to have right, title and Ajay Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165678085/
1 interest over the part of the property by way of sale deed executed by one Jojona Saha in favour of complainant on 20.02.1976 and after the said purchase, the land was duly mutated vide Mutation Case No.136 of 1979-80.

sentences.text: 5. It is alleged that the employees of M/s Rungta Mines to which accused no.4 is one of the Directors had illegally purchased the said land.

6. The complainant is aggrieved by execution of two sale deed on 17.07.2008 being sale deed no.5729/4862 and sale deed no.8438/7116 dated 16.10.2008 respectively by this petitioner on the basis of power of attorney executed by Gobindo Nayak.
Since the sale deed was executed by this petitioner in favour of M/s Rungta Mines.
Director of said Company has also been impleaded as accused.
ARGUMENT OF PETITIONER 7.
It is submitted that the petitioner had executed sale deed on the basis of power of attorney executed by Gobindo Nayak (A-1) and Dilip Kumar Giri (A-2).

The sum and substance of the submission advanced on behalf of petitioner is that land in question was duly executed in favour of Gobindo Nayak (A-1) and Dilip Kumar Giri (A-2) and it was duly mutated in the name of predecessor in interest of the power of attorney holder.

There was no criminality on the part of the petitioner in execution of the sale deed as he was bonafide power-of-attorney holder in whose name the land had been duly mutated and he was paying rent to the state after being accepted as a tenant.

Even if it is assumed that he had no title to dispose of the land no criminal offence will be made out as it will not amount to cause any wrongful loss to the complainant .the person aggrieved can be the purchaser of the land and not the so-called owner of the said land .Reliance is placed on the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohammed Ibrahim & Others Vs. State of Bihar & Another,
(2009) 8 SCC 751.

entities.text:
Mohammed Ibrahim & Others Vs. State of Bihar & Another,
(2009) 8 SCC 751
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that even if the petitioner has no right to execute the sale of deed,
only party who can aggrieved of such dispossession of the land, will be purchaser of land nor title holder of the land.
8. The learned APP assisted by the counsel on behalf of the Complainant have opposed the quashing petition.
It is submitted that the sale deed was executed by the petitioner who was not the titleholder nor the power-of-attorney was executed in his favour by the owner of the said land.
ANALYSIS 9.

The sum and substance of the Complainant's case is that he was the real owner of the land whereas the sale deed has been executed by the Petitioner who had power-of-attorney from a person not the owner of the said land in question.

Without entering into the rival submissions regarding the ownership of the land in question, even if it is assumed that the petitioner had no title to sell the land, the only party who can be said to have been cheated will be the purchaser and not the complainant.
The law in this regard is settled in Mohammed Ibrahim (supra) which does not require further reiteration in this regard.
This Court is of the view that on the averments made in the Complaint Petition no prima facie offence will be made out and it will be an abuse of process to permit as continuation.
